summary: Session cache coherence delay causes p99 latency spikes for identical conversational turns
description:
Issue summary:
WriteRight.ai observed sudden p99 latency spikes (up to 6s) for identical conversational turns that previously returned in <200ms. Occurred intermittently across sessions that replay previously-seen user turns.

Impact:
- Affects ~12% of Generate calls for a subset of customers on Dedicated pools in us-east.
- Customer reports degraded UX for their conversation replay feature and increased timeouts in client.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (cluster: rw-dedicated-3), prod us-east, model: redwood-7b-instruct-v1, serving-runtime v3.14.2.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Boot a session with conversation history of ~6 turns.
2) Send an identical user turn that previously produced a cached prefix path.
3) Observe response times: some requests return ~150ms, others spike to 4–6s or timeout.

Observed vs Expected:
- Observed: high variance, repeated identical turns sometimes hit high p99 latency and occasional 504s.
- Expected: stable low latency due to prefix/KV cache warm hits for identical prefixes.

Initial logs & errors:
- Gateway shows request completed but backend processing extended (see serving-runtime traces).
- No obvious 5xx from api-gateway. Some 504s correlate with backend queue growth.
- Sample trace IDs: trace-20260310-0451, trace-20260310-0815 (attached).

Notes: Customer supplied session IDs and example payloads; they requested urgent review due to production impact.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Aisha): Acknowledged. Escalating to SRE and runtime team; gathering traces and sample payloads from customer.
2026-03-10 10:03 - SRE (Marco): Reproduced locally on rw-dedicated-3 with a replay harness. Observed KV cache miss rate correlated with high latency. Opening deeper investigation.

2026-03-10 14:21 - Runtime Eng (Lena): Hypothesis: delayed prefix tombstone reaping / stale mapping causing cache coherence window where lookups fall back to cold KV shard reads and synchronous prefetch, which stalls token generation.
2026-03-11 08:55 - Support (Aisha): Customer confirmed spike frequency dropped after small traffic pattern change (shorter bursts) — suggests race under specific load patterns.

2026-03-12 16:40 - Runtime Eng (Marco): Patch deployed to rw-dedicated-3 that reduces tombstone reaper pause and forces asynchronous prefetch for fallback path. Monitoring telemetry; customer reports latency normalized.
2026-03-12 18:02 - Support (Aisha): Customer confirmed resolution and requested postmortem notes. Marking ticket resolved pending follow-up doc.
investigation_notes: Reproduction: used customer payloads; load generator mimicked 60 sessions with intermittent identical turn replays. p99 latency spikes reproduced within 30 minutes.
Telemetry: KV cache hit ratio dropped from 98% to 65% during spike windows. Backend queue depth increased ~3x during those windows.
Tracing: spans show synchronous cold-kv fetch on fallback path took 1200–1800ms, plus blocking on KV shard mutexes when multiple concurrent requests targeted same shard.

Root cause hypothesis: tombstone reaper runs with a pause/backoff heuristic that, under bursty session-replay patterns, left index mappings in an intermediate state. Concurrent lookups raced with a synchronous fallback that performed blocking shard reads and synchronous prefetch, amplifying latency (thundering behavior).
Additional finding: scheduler's prefetch task rate limiter sometimes starved asynchronous prefetch tasks, causing more requests to take the synchronous cold path.
Risk assessment: high for dedicated pools with chat replay features; moderate for hosted pools due to different shard allocation and lower per-customer density.

Decision: implement two mitigations: 1) make tombstone reaper backoff more conservative and add a fast-path for stable prefix mappings; 2) change fallback prefetch to be asynchronous+rate-limited with best-effort timeout so generation doesn't block indefinitely.
resolution: Hotfix applied (2026-03-12): tombstone reaper backoff reduced and reaper run stagger randomized to avoid simultaneous map holes across shards.

Hotfix applied (2026-03-12): fallback prefetch converted to asynchronous best-effort prefetch with a 250ms soft timeout; on timeout, generation proceeds using a partial KV result to avoid long stalls.
Post-deploy observation: KV hit ratio returned to ~97%; p99 latency for the repro harness dropped from ~4.5s to ~210ms. No regressions observed in end-to-end tests.
Customer communication: Support notified WriteRight.ai of root cause and fixes, recommended configuration tweaks (session burst smoothing) as a short-term safeguard.

Follow-up actions: Create a confluence doc for KV reaper heuristics, add unit/integration tests for concurrent shard fallback, and schedule a dedicated stress test for replay patterns (owner: Marco Chen).
